body: Willow is Capcom's NES action role-playing adaptation of the fantasy film, following Willow Ufgood on a journey through villages, forests and dangerous passages. He fights with a sword, protects himself with a shield and learns magic while searching for a way to defeat evil. The overhead viewpoint gives the journey a continuous geography to explore. Encounters with inhabitants provide advice and equipment, allowing the film's world to become a place that the player gradually learns to navigate through conversation and action.

Enemies are fought in real time, and experience increases Willow's level as the adventure continues. Weapons, shields and spells expand his abilities, with items discovered during exploration rather than purchased through a money system. A visit to a house can therefore matter as much as a victory outside town. The next useful discovery may be a piece of advice or a new means of surviving an encounter. Progress involves connecting those small findings to the dangers waiting along the route.

Capcom also produced a Willow arcade game in 1989, using side-scrolling action and a different structure. The NES adventure instead gives Willow an extended journey largely undertaken alone, with passwords allowing progress to be resumed. Its relationship to the film leaves room for the slower work of exploring and developing a character. Harumi Fujita's music accompanies that change in pace. The adaptation finds its own shape by making the hero's growing abilities, and the places where they are needed, part of one connected expedition.
